title: Great-circle thrackleable trees are a proper subclass of augmented caterpillars
source: Karen Collins and Cleo Roberts, “Great-circle Tree Thrackles”, arXiv:2110.09679 (2021); Discrete Math. 346(1) (2023) 113121; Conjecture 3.4. https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.09679

significance.root_decision: The conjecture holds: every great-circle thrackleable tree (with at least three vertices) is an augmented caterpillar, and the containment is proper. The open half is strictness. The 14-vertex tree T formed by an edge 01 with three pendant 2-paths at each of 0 and 1 is an augmented caterpillar under every reading of the source's Definition 3.1 (its legs are disjoint paths), but it has no great-circle thrackle drawing in general position. The proof (GPT-6.1 Sol) encodes a drawing by the signs of 3×3 determinants of the vertex vectors (a rank-3 chirotope), imposes the 3-term Grassmann–Plücker relations and an exact table saying when a short or long great-circle arc meets another exactly once, and refutes the resulting 162,578-clause formula with an LRAT certificate; the containment half (the source's Theorem 3.2) is re-proved the same way from a certificate that the 3,3,3 spider is undrawable. Lean defines drawings on the unit sphere of ℝ³ in general position, short and long arcs, the thrackle condition (every two distinct edges meet in exactly one point) and the source's Definition 3.1 with legs, generates the input clauses by a Lean function of the tree, proves that every geometric drawing satisfies all of them, and checks both certificates by `decide +kernel` through a reflective RUP checker proved sound in Lean (no native_decide, no bv_decide, no ofReduceBool). T is the tree the source's own Conjecture 3.5 predicts is undrawable; that conjecture is neither used nor proved.
significance.caveat: Both halves are stated for trees with at least three vertices: under the literal Definition 3.1, K₁ and K₂ are drawable but not augmented caterpillars (proved in Lean), so the source's own Theorem 3.2 needs the same restriction; the open strictness half is unaffected. The MathDB paraphrase omits 'general position', which the source assumes by convention. The strictness half is a certified finite computation by the standard oriented-matroid-plus-SAT method in its spherical setting; once the encoding exists a SAT sweep finds such trees quickly. Cross-model reviewer: not routine 0.55 (at the floor root uses for counting); final checker 0.5–0.55, COUNTS as a borderline, modest result. The conjecture has no citing works, so 'open' is weak evidence of difficulty. Journal text (Discrete Math. 2023) unread. Because GPT-6.1 Sol hit its usage limit, the Lean packaging and the final check were both by Claude Opus 5.5 lanes (the cross-model review is the Opus review of a Sol proof). The same conjecture is MathDB 247589; it counts once.

root_basis: Root (Claude Opus 5.5) extracted the 43 modules from the appendix into an empty directory, rebuilt and kernel-checked them (all exit 0, axioms exactly the allowed three for all three endpoints, no forbidden tokens), and compared S2, shortArc, longArc, GeneralPosition, IsGCThrackleDrawing, IsAugmentedCaterpillar and Conjecture34 with the endpoint written by the Claude Opus referee: same arcs and thrackle condition (exists-unique instead of ncard = 1), general position stated literally with a proved determinant bridge, augmented caterpillar with the legs clause of Definition 3.1 added explicitly (stronger, proved for the witness and as the containment conclusion), both halves restricted to trees with at least three vertices.
